key_insight: Spectrum-resolved Hong-Ou-Mandel interference turns photon spectral structure into a trainable resource, enabling a compact optical actor-critic that supports continuous-action reinforcement learning.
engineering_relevance: The approach suggests a photonic path to smaller, potentially more sample-efficient controllers for continuous control and online quantum hardware calibration.
method: Promote HOM coincidence spectra from a scalar readout to a spectrum-resolved computational feature map.
Use diagonal spectral responses to generate continuous actions in the actor.
Use higher-order spectral correlations as nonlinear state-action features for the critic/value estimate.
evidence_signal: Across five continuous-control benchmarks, SR-HOM beat parameter-matched MLP baselines, including a 4.4× sample-efficiency gain and a 74.0% higher best 100-episode moving-average return on LunarLanderContinuous-v3; in gate-calibration simulations it restored fidelities to 0.9917 (CZ) and 0.9952 (iSWAP).
watch_item: The reported gains are based on simulations and benchmark tasks, so real-world photonic noise, hardware drift, and readout complexity may reduce performance.
paper_title: Quantum Optical Reinforcement Learning via Spectrum-Resolved Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
